Both of the Petitions were admitted by the Commission. The Commission directed that the parties shall maintain the status quo in regard to connectivity granted to the Petitioners herein. ## ** Submission of Respondent, CTUIL in Petition No. 453/MP/2025 and 455/MP/2025) ** Order in Petition 453/MP/2025 along with IA No. 39/2025 and Petition No. 455/MP/2025 along with IA No. 41/2025 submit land documents in the name of its subsidiary to CTUIL. The reliance of the Petitioner on this Commission’s Order dated 12.07.2024 in Petition No. 192/MP/2024 to state that generic directions regarding acceptance of documents have not been complied with by CTUIL is devoid of any merit and substance and is liable to be categorically rejected. _“Learned counsel for the Petitioners submitted that the present Petitions have been filed invoking the Commission’s Power to Relax and Power to Remove Difficulties under the GNA Regulations, 2022 and the consequent directions upon CTUIL to accept the land documents/documents towards fulfilment of condition subsequent under Regulation 11A (1) & (2) in the name of subsidiary company for the utilisation of connectivity granted to a parent company. Learned counsel submitted that the issue involved in these cases is squarely covered by the order dated 12.7.2024 in Petition No. 192/MP/2024 (ACME Solar Holdings Pvt. Ltd. & Anr. v. CTUIL), wherein a similar relaxation has already been allowed by the Commission. Learned counsel also urged the Commission to pass a generic direction to CTUIL to accept the relevant land documents in the name of subsidiary company for the purpose of connectivity granted to the parent company as had been passed vide Record of Proceedings for the hearing dated 29.1.2025 in Petition No. 147/MP/2025 (SAEL Industries Limited v. CTUIL) in the context of accepting the_ Order in Petition 453/MP/2025 along with IA No. 39/2025 and Petition No. 455/MP/2025 along with IA No. 41/2025 _2. After hearing the learned counsel for the Petitioner, the Commission observed that the issue of submissions of land documents by the subsidiary is under consideration in the Draft third amendment to the Central Electricity Regulatory Commission (Connectivity and General Network Access to the inter-State Transmission System) Regulations. Accordingly,_ **_the Commission directed CTUIL to process the land documents in the name of subsidiary where Connectivity have been granted to the Parent company or vice versa, to comply with Regulation 11A (1) of the GNA Regulations, for all such cases, till the issuance of the third amendment to the GNA Regulations, subject to necessary verification whether the entity with land documents is a subsidiary company under the Company's Act. In view of the above, the Commission also directed the Petitioners to file an affidavit indicating the survival of their grievance(s), as raised in the instant case, within two weeks_** _._ Order in Petition 453/MP/2025 along with IA No. 39/2025 and Petition No. 455/MP/2025 along with IA No. 41/2025 15. We have considered the submissions of the Petitioners and the Respondent. The issue in the instant Petitions is the submission of land documents in the name of the SPV/subsidiary (i.e. Petitioner No. 2 in the instant Petitions) where the Parent company (i.e. Petitioner No. 1 in the instant Petitions) is the Connectivity Grantee, for compliance of Regulation 11A(1) of the GNA Regulations. Order in Petition 453/MP/2025 along with IA No. 39/2025 and Petition No. 455/MP/2025 along with IA No. 41/2025 Order in Petition 453/MP/2025 along with IA No. 39/2025 and Petition No. 455/MP/2025 along with IA No. 41/2025 21. Accordingly, the prayer of Petitioners in Petition No. 455/MP/2025 to direct CTUIL to accept the documents towards fulfilment of conditions subsequent under Regulations 11A(2) in the name of Petitioner No. 2, where the Connectivity grantee is the Parent company, i.e., Petitioner No. 1 has already been addressed.
